ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r8.claim: The narrative suppresses an intervening step: Moses and Aaron took their message to Pharaoh before his question about their Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p39/r8.anchor: Moses (sws) and Aaron (sws) took the message they

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r1.claim: Pharaoh implies that he himself is Lord, asking whose messengers Moses and Aaron could be.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r1.anchor: since he himself was the Lord, then whose messengers were they

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r2.claim: Pharaoh was treated in Egypt as a god-king and solar avatar, with his idols and statues worshipped throughout the land.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r2.anchor: He was regarded as the avatar of the sun

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r3.claim: Pharaoh's question is sarcastic: Israelites did not accept him as God, although their own God seemed absent from practical affairs while Pharaoh controlled them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r3.anchor: did not regard him to be so

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r4.claim: Moses and Aaron presented Israel's God as a living being making demands and warning Pharaoh, which he found strange.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p40/r4.anchor: presented God as a living being before the Pharaoh

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.claim: The passage teaches all callers to divine unity, especially the Prophet, to keep trusting God under every condition, using episodes from Moses's life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r1.anchor: Bu âyetlerde, başta Resûl-i Ekrem olmak üzere Allah’ın birliği inancına çağrıda bulunacak bütün tebliğ insanlarına, hangi şartlar altında olursa olsun, Allah’a olan güveni bir an bile yitirmemek gerektiği fikri, Hz. Mûsâ’nın hayatından kesitler verilerek telkin edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.claim: When Pharaoh mockingly asked who their Lord was, Moses answered that God gives every creature its nature and form and then guides it, so all owe their existence to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r11.anchor: Mûsâ O’nun evrendeki her şeyi özüyle ve biçimiyle var eden sonra da her varlığa yolunu yordamını gösteren Allah olduğunu söylemiş, böylece Firavun da dahil olmak üzere her şeyin varlığını O’na borçlu olduğuna dikkat çekmişti.

QASHANI:20:48-51/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:48-51/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:48-51/r2.claim: Pharaoh’s question about the Lord indicates the self’s veiling from its Lord.
QASHANI:20:48-51/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى احتجاب النفس من جناب الرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r4.claim: The narrative resumes with Pharaoh's question to both brothers, though he addresses Moses alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r4.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره فأتيا فرعون وقالا له ما أمرهما الله أن يبلغاه قال فمن ربكما يا موسى خاطبهما معا وأفرد بالنداء موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Moses alone is addressed because he was the chief of the mission and had the more honored signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: إذ كان صاحب عظم الرسالة وكريم الآيات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls Moses the source of prophethood and Aaron his minister and follower; Pharaoh may also have sought Moses because Aaron was eloquent while Moses had a speech impediment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p339/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري لأنه الأصل في النبوة وهارون وزيره وتابعه، ويحتمل أن يحمله خبثه وذعارته على استدعاء كلام موسى دون كلام أخيه

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r12.claim: The question addresses both Moses and Aaron, then singles out Moses by name; the change may match the verse endings.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r12.anchor: { فمن ربكما } على التثنية ، ثم قال : { يا موسى }

QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r13.claim: Alternatively, Moses is named because he held precedence over Aaron.
QUSHAYRI:v2p263/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن موسى كان مقدما على هارون فخصه بالنداء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r1.claim: The omitted exchange is compressed for brevity, implying Moses and Aaron promptly obeyed and their words to Pharaoh needed no explicit retelling.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r1.anchor: بعد ما اتياه وبلغاه ما امرا به وإنما طوى ذكر ذلك للايجاز والأشعار بأنهما كما امرا بذلك سارعا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the brothers waited at Pharaoh’s gate for a time before admission, then entered after a severe screen was lifted.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنهما لما أمر اباتيانه وقول ما ذكر له جاءا جميعا إلى بابه فاقاما حينا لا يؤذن لهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r3.claim: Wahb reports Moses’ fearless entry among trained lions, the staff becoming a serpent and killing many, Pharaoh’s request for a forty-day delay, and the lions escorting Moses out.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r3.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه أن الله تعالى لما أمر موسى عليه السلام بما أمر أقبل إلى فرعون في مدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r4.claim: Aaron was apparently with Moses at the encounter; the Wahb report may omit him because it focuses on Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r4.anchor: واظاهر أن هرون كان معه حين الآيتان ولعله إنما لم يذكر في هذا الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r5.claim: One report says Asiya urged acceptance of the brothers’ call, while Haman opposed it as a loss of mastery and lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r5.anchor: شاور آسية فقالت ما ينبغي لأحد أن يرد ما دعيا إليه فشاور هامان وكان لا يبت أمرا دون رايه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r6.claim: For such stories, rely on revelation and disregard other accounts unless their soundness is established.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r6.anchor: والأولى في أمثال هذه القصص الاكتفاء بما في المنزل وعدم الالتفات إلى غيره إلا أن يوثق بصحته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r7.claim: The Wahb account’s forty-day reprieve conflicts with Moses later setting the festival day as the appointment; the encounter apparently did not happen twice.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r7.anchor: فإن كون فرعون جعل الأجل يعكر عليه ما سيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى من قول موسى عليه السلام حين طلب منه فرعون أن يجعل موعدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r8.claim: The question is an explanatory resumption: the text supplies what Pharaoh said after the brothers delivered their message.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p199#2/r8.anchor: والجملة استئناف بياني كأنه قيل فماذا قال حين أتياه وقالا له ما قالا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r1.claim: Pharaoh does not call God his own Lord, even while quoting the brothers’ words, because of his extreme arrogance and tyranny.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r1.anchor: لغاية عتوه ونهاية طغيانه بل اضافه اليهما لما أن المرسل لابد أن يكون ربا للرسول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r2.claim: Another explanation is that the brothers had already declared God Lord of all, while naming Pharaoh’s lordship alone sufficed for the immediate point.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r2.anchor: وقيل : لأنهما قد صرحا بربوبيته تعالى للكل بأن قالا : انا رسول رب العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r3.claim: The prefixed fa makes Pharaoh’s question follow from the brothers’ claim to be messengers of their Lord: he asks who sent them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r3.anchor: والفاء لترتيب السؤال على ما سبق من كونهما رسولي ربهما أي إذا كنتما رسولي ربكما الذي ارسلكما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r4.claim: Pharaoh addresses Moses alone because he recognizes him as the principal messenger and Aaron as his minister.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r4.anchor: وتخصيص النداء بموسى عليه السلام مع توجيه الخطاب اليهما لما ظهر له من أنه الأصل في الرسالة وهرون وزيره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r5.claim: A further possibility is that Pharaoh taunts Moses as his own dependent, recalling that he raised him as a child.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون للتعريض بأنه ربه كما قال : الم نربك فينا وليدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r6.claim: Some exegetes say Pharaoh knew Moses had a speech impediment and wanted to silence him; this assumes the impediment persisted to some degree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p200/r6.anchor: لأنه قد عرف أن له عليه السلام رتة فاراد أن يسكتة وهو مبنى على ما عليه كثير من المفسرين من بقاء رتة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.claim: Pharaoh asks who the deity is that sent Moses and Aaron.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r1.claim: The narrative omits that Moses and Aaron first delivered their message to Pharaoh, since the context implies they obeyed and did what they were commanded.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r1.anchor: فإن المطيع إذا أمر بشيء فعله لا محالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r2.claim: Pharaoh addressed both brothers but called Moses because Moses was the principal and Aaron his minister and follower.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r2.anchor: وإنما خاطب الإثنين وخص موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام بالنداء لأنه الأصل وهرون وزيره وتابعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r3.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh knew Moses stammered and Aaron spoke eloquently, and wanted to silence Moses, as his later boast suggests.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:49/r3.anchor: أو لأنه عرف أن له رتة ولأخيه فصاحة فأراد أن يفحمه ويدل عليه قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r6.claim: Pharaoh chooses debate rather than force so that he will not be accused of foolishness and ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r6.anchor: أي فرعون مدافعا لهما بالمناظرة لا بالبطش , لئلا ينسب إلى السفه والجهل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r7.claim: By asking who their Lord is rather than asking about his own Lord, Pharaoh evades fair consideration and redirects the question to expose them to humiliation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r7.anchor: حيدة عن سواء النظر وصرفا للكالم على الوجه الموضح لخزيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r8.claim: Moses is singled out because he is the principal in the mission, although Pharaoh had addressed both messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p22/r8.anchor: ولما كان موسى عليه السلام هو الأصل في ذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r3.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r3.claim: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh, waited outside before being admitted, announced that they were God's messengers, and Pharaoh asked Moses who their Lord was.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r3.anchor: فانطلقا جميعا إلى فرعون فأقاما ببابه حينا لا يؤذن لهما ثم أذن لهما بعد حجاب شديد فقالا: {إنا رسولا ربك} فقال: {فمن ربكما يا موسى}

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r4.claim: Moses demanded that Pharaoh believe in God and release the Israelites, but Pharaoh refused and demanded a sign.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r4.anchor: قال: أريد أن تؤمن بالله وترسل معي بني إسرائيل فأبى عليه ذلك وقال: ائت بآية إن كنت من الصادقين

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r5.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r5.claim: Moses's staff became a huge open-mouthed serpent that rushed toward Pharaoh, who fled his throne and begged Moses to stop it.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r5.anchor: فألقى بعصاه فتحولت حية عظيمة فاغرة فاها مسرعة إلى فرعون

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r6.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r6.claim: Moses took the serpent away and displayed a white hand; the report identifies the whiteness as leprosy, which disappeared when he returned his hand to his sleeve.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r6.anchor: واستغاث بموسى: أن يكفها عنه ففعل وأخرج يده من جيبه بيضاء من غير سوء) يعني برص

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r7.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r7.claim: Pharaoh's chiefs called Moses and Aaron magicians aiming to expel the Egyptians and take their exemplary way, meaning their kingdom and comfortable life.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r7.anchor: فقالوا له: {هذان لساحران يريدان أن يخرجاكم من أرضكم بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى} يعنون ملكهم الذي هم فيه والعيش

DURR-FULL:v5p573/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r8.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r8.claim: The chiefs refused Moses's request and advised Pharaoh to gather the numerous magicians in the land to defeat the brothers' magic.
DURR-FULL:v5p573/r8.anchor: فأبوا على موسى أن يعطوه شيئا مما طلب وقالوا له: اجمع لهم السحرة - فإنهم بأرضنا كثير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r4.claim: The speech is God's instruction to Moses and Aaron; its attribution is confirmed by the narrative transition to Pharaoh's question, and this stretch of the story had not appeared in earlier surahs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r4.anchor: وهذا كله كلام الله الذي أمرهما بتبليغه إلى فرعون ، كما يدل لذلك تعقيبه بقوله تعالى : قال فمن ربكما يا موسى } ( طه : 49 ) على أسلوب حكاية المحاورات . وما ذكر من أول القصة إلى هنا لم يتقدم في السور الماضية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r5.claim: Pharaoh's question answers the message Moses and Aaron were ordered to deliver; omitted narrative steps are inferred: they came and delivered it, then he asked who their Lord was.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r5.anchor: هذا حكاية جواب فرعون عن الكلام الذي أمر الله موسى وهارون بإبلاغه فرعون ، ففي الآية حذف جمل دل عليها السياق قصدا للإيجاز . والتقدير : فأتياه فقالا له ما أمرا به ، فقال : فمن ربكما ؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r6.claim: Pharaoh's question is separated as part of the Quran's established style for narrating dialogue, discussed elsewhere including 2:30 onward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r6.anchor: ولذلك جاءت حكاية قول فرعون بجملة مفصولة على طريقة حكاية المحاورات التي استقريناها من أسلوب القرآن وبيناها في سورة البقرة وغيرها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r7.claim: Pharaoh addresses both with the dual pronoun but calls Moses alone because he knows Moses is the principal messenger and Aaron follows; Moses' upbringing in the palace gave him prior access, and Moses likely spoke while Aaron affirmed him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p230/r7.anchor: ووجه فرعون الخطاب إليهما بالضمير المشترك ، ثم خص موسى بالإقبال عليه بالنداء ، لعلمه بأن موسى هو الأصل بالرسالة وأن هارون تابع له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r1.claim: The phrase our Lord is tied to their dual pronoun because they had told Pharaoh that they were messengers of his Lord in 20:47.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r1.anchor: وإضافته الرب إلى ضميرهما لأنهما قالا له إنا رسولا ربك } ( طه : 47 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r2.claim: Pharaoh asks about their Lord instead of saying my Lord to avoid acknowledging God's lordship, lest his followers think he doubts his own deity or admits having a lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r2.anchor: وأعرض عن أن يقول : فمن ربي ؟ إلى قوله { فمن ربكما } إعراضا عن الاعتراف بالمربوبية ولو بحكاية قولهما ، لئلا يقع ذلك في سمع أتباعه وقومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r3.claim: Moses answers because Pharaoh singled him out by name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p232/r3.anchor: وتولى موسى الجواب لأنه خص بالسؤال بسبب النداء له دون غيره .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r8.claim: Although Pharaoh says Lord of you two, he singles out Moses by name to distinguish and confront him as the chief messenger and bearer of the signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p46#2/r8.anchor: وقوله يا موسى بعد جمعه مع هارون في الضمير، نداء بمعنى التخصيص والتوقيف إذ كان صاحب عظم الرسالة ولزيم الآيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the omitted words as ‘they went to him and delivered the message’; the question itself shows that they had come and spoken.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p291/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج و إنما لم يقل فأتياه لأن في الكلام دليلا على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh asks who sent and commissioned Moses, denying that he knows this Creator and claiming no deity besides himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p297#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى مخبرا عن فرعون أنه قال لموسى منكرا وجود الصانع الخالق، إله كل شيء وربه ومليكه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r1.claim: Pharaoh asks both prophets but directs the challenge to Moses because Moses is the principal prophet and Aaron his minister and follower.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r1.anchor: خاطب الاثنين ، ووجه النداء إلى أحدهما وهو موسى ؛ لأنه الأصل في النبوة ، وهارون وزيره وتابعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r2.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh's malice made him demand Moses' speech, knowing Aaron's eloquence and Moses' speech impediment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p68/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يحمله خبثه ودعارته على استدعاء كلام موسى دون كلام أخيه

MUQATIL:20:48-53/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:48-53/r2.claim: Pharaoh asks Moses who their Lord is.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p57/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57/r1.claim: Pharaoh addresses both Moses and Aaron, then singles out Moses because he is the principal prophet while Aaron follows him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p57/r1.anchor: خاطبهما ثم بادي احدهما لأن موسى هو الأصل في النبوة وهرون نابعه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r11.claim: Pharaoh names Moses alone for the verse endings; another explanation is that Moses alone bore the message, speech, and sign.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r11.anchor: ذكر فرعون موسى دون هارون لرؤوس الآي. وقيل: خصصه بالذكر لأنه صاحب الرسالة والكلام والآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r12.claim: Although Moses speaks, both brothers delivered the message: one speaks at a time and the other supports him when he finishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r12.anchor: إنهما جميعا بلغا الرسالة وإن كان ساكتا لأنه في وقت الكلام إنما يتكلم واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r13.claim: When two people are jointly entrusted with a task, one may perform it while the other is present and both fulfill the charge and merit reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r13.anchor: أن الاثنين إذا قلدا أمرا فقام به أحدهما، والآخر شخصه هناك موجود مستغنى عنه في وقت دون وقت

QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r14.claim: The commands to both brothers to go and speak, followed by Pharaoh addressing Moses while Aaron was present, establish that both performed their commission.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:47-50/r14.anchor: فأمرهما جميعا بالذهاب وبالقول، ثم أعلمنا في وقت الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r1.claim: Although Pharaoh was powerful, Moses answered his challenge by debating rather than using force; Pharaoh avoided violence first because it would expose him to the charge of ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r1.anchor: أن فرعون كان شديد القوة عظيم الغلبة كثير العسكر ثم إن موسى عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r2.claim: Razi infers that even ignorant Pharaoh would not accept foolishness without proof, making such conduct still less fitting for a claimant to Islam and learning.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r2.anchor: فاستنكف من ذلك وشرع أولا في المناظرة وذلك يدل على أن السفاهة من غير الحجة شيء ما كان يرتضيه فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r3.claim: Moses’ proof of the Creator before establishing his prophethood shows that blind imitation is invalid, as knowledge of God must precede knowledge of a messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r3.anchor: واشتغل بإقامة الدلالة على وجود الصانع وذلك يدل على فساد التقليد

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r4.claim: Razi rejects the Taʿlimiyya claim that knowledge of God is obtained from a messenger’s statement, since Moses first establishes God’s existence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r4.anchor: ويدل أيضا على فساد قول التعليمية الذين يقولون نستفيد معرفة الإله من قول الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r5.claim: Razi also rejects the Hashwiyya claim that knowledge of God and religion comes from scripture and Sunnah, since this exchange establishes God first.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r5.anchor: وتدل على فساد قول الحشوية الذين يقولون نستفيد معرفة الله والدين من الكتاب والسنة

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r6.claim: The verse permits quoting a false opponent’s words, as the Qur’an quotes Pharaoh and deniers of prophethood and resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r6.anchor: تدل الآية على أنه يجوز حكاية كلام المبطل لأنه تعالى حكى كلام فرعون في إنكاره الإله

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r7.claim: When presenting a question, one must also give its answer so that doubt does not remain, as God does in these passages.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r7.anchor: إلا أنه يجب أنك متى أوردت السؤال فاقرنه بالجواب لئلا يبقى الشك كما فعل الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r8.claim: A person in the right must hear and answer a false opponent without harming or alienating him, as Moses did with Pharaoh.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r8.anchor: دلت الآية على أن المحق يجب عليه استماع كلام المبطل والجواب عنه من غير إيذاء ولا إيحاش

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r9.claim: Razi links this conduct to the command to invite people with wisdom and good admonition.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r9.anchor: كما أمر الله تعالى رسوله في قوله : { ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة } ( النحل : 125 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r10.claim: Razi also cites the command to grant a polytheist protection until he hears God’s word.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55/r10.anchor: وقال : { وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله } ( التوبة : 6 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.claim: Some say Pharaoh knew God but publicly denied Him through arrogance, oppression, and falsehood; they offer six arguments.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r1.anchor: فقيل إنه كان عارفا إلا أنه كان يظهر الإنكار تكبرا وتجبرا وزورا وبهتانا

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.claim: They cite Moses’ statement that Pharaoh knew the signs came from the Lord of the heavens and earth, and the report that deniers inwardly recognized them (17:102; 27:14).
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r2.anchor: قوله : { لقد علمت ما أنزل هؤلاء إلا رب * السماوات والارض } ( الإسراء : 102 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.claim: They argue that Pharaoh was rational and accountable, and any rational person knows he came into being after nonexistence and therefore needs a governor.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r3.anchor: أنه كان عاقلا وإلا لم يجز تكليفه وكل من كان عاقلا قد علم بالضرورة أنه وجد بعد العدم

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r5.claim: They read Pharaoh’s and his people’s belief that they would not return to God as evidence that they knew the Creator but denied resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r5.anchor: ورابعها : قوله في سورة القصص في صفة فرعون وقومه وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r6.claim: They argue Pharaoh’s rule did not extend beyond Egypt, and Moses’ safe escape to Midian makes it implausible that Pharaoh thought himself lord of the universe.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r6.anchor: أن ملك فرعون لم يتجاوز القبط ولم يبلغ الشام ولما هرب موسى عليه السلام إلى مدين قال له شعيب : { لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين } ( القصص : 25 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r7.claim: They say Pharaoh asked about the Lord’s essence, not existence: Moses described the Lord of heaven and earth, and Pharaoh replied that the messenger was mad rather than disputing existence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r7.anchor: أنه لما قال : { وما رب العالمين } قال موسى عليه السلام : { رب * السماوات والارض * وما بينهما } ( الشعراء : 24 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r8.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r8.claim: Others say Pharaoh was ignorant of God, while agreeing that a rational person could not think himself creator of the heavens, earth, sun, moon, or himself.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r8.anchor: ومن الناس من قال إنه كان جاهلا بربه واتفقوا على أن العاقل لا يجوز أن يعتقد في نفسه أنه خالق هذه السموات والأرضين

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r9.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r9.claim: One proposed form of Pharaoh’s ignorance is that he was a materialist who denied any effective cause.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r9.anchor: فيحتمل أنه كان دهريا نافيا للمؤثر أصلا

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r10.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r10.claim: Another proposed form is that he was a philosopher who affirmed a necessary causal principle.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أنه كان فلسفيا قائلا بالعلة لموجبه

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r11.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r11.claim: Another possibility is that Pharaoh worshipped the stars.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r11.anchor: ويحتمل أنه كان من عبدة الكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r12.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r12.claim: Another possibility is that he belonged to the incarnationist corporealist sect.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أنه كان من الحلولية المجسمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r13.claim: Razi explains Pharaoh’s claim to lordship as a demand that subjects obey and submit to him rather than obey anyone else.
RAZI-FULL:v22p55#2/r13.anchor: وأما ادعاؤه الربوبية لنفسه فبمعنى أنه يجب عليهم طاعته والانقياد له وعدم الاشتغال بطاعة غيره

RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r1.claim: The Taha question asks who the Lord is, while the Shuʿara question asks what the Lord is; Razi says the first naturally precedes the second.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r1.anchor: السؤال ههنا بمن وهو عن الكيفية وفي سورة الشعراء بما وهو عن الماهية وهما سؤالان مختلفان

RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r2.claim: Razi’s preferred sequence is that Pharaoh first claimed lordship and asked who Moses’ Lord was; after Moses made God’s existence undeniable, Pharaoh shifted to the difficult question of essence, which humans cannot know.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r2.anchor: والأقرب أن يقال سؤال من كان مقدما على سؤال ما لأنه كان يقول إني أنا الله والرب

RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r3.claim: Pharaoh says Lord rather than God because he had claimed to be Moses’ lord by raising him; this is a rhetorical challenge about competing uses of lordship.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r3.anchor: إنما قال : { فمن ربكما } ولم يقل فمن إلهكما لأنه أثبت نفسه ربا في قوله : { ألم نربك فينا وليدا

RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r4.claim: Razi compares Pharaoh’s equivocation to Nimrod’s: Abraham’s claim that God gives life and death differed in meaning from Nimrod’s verbal counterclaim, just as divine lordship differs from raising Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v22p56/r4.anchor: وهذا الكلام شبيه بكلام نمروذ لأن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما قال : { ربي الذى يحى ويميت } ( البقرة : 258 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.claim: Razi offers two reasons Pharaoh addressed both Moses and Aaron but then singled out Moses: Moses was the principal prophet and Aaron his minister, or Pharaoh exploited Moses’ stutter and Aaron’s greater eloquence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r1.anchor: أن فرعون خاطب الاثنين بقوله : { فمن ربكما } ثم وجه النداء إلى أحدهما وهو موسى عليه السلام لأنه الأصل في النبوة وهرون وزيره وتابعه

RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r2.claim: For the second explanation, Razi cites Pharaoh’s claim that Moses was contemptible and could barely speak clearly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p58/r2.anchor: ويدل عليه قوله : { أم أنا خير من هاذا الذى هو مهين ولا يكاد يبين } ( الزخرف : 52 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r1.claim: Moses answers the question about God with a concise proof because it calls for reasoning, but refers the question about earlier generations to the Knower of the unseen because it calls for transmitted information he lacks.
RAZI-FULL:v22p59/r1.anchor: وكان ذلك مما سبيله الإستدلال أجاب بما هو الصواب بأوجز عبارة وأحسن معنى

STUDYQURAN:20:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r1.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī sees Pharaoh's question as an initial stage of a deeper theological inquiry, continued in 26:23.
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r1.anchor: Al-Rāzī notes that the question posed by Pharaoh here was a preliminary stage to his deeper inquiry about God

STUDYQURAN:20:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r2.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r2.claim: Other commentators reject a serious theological reading and take Pharaoh's questions as confrontation.
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r2.anchor: Other commentators reject the idea that Pharaoh was making a serious theological inquiry into the Nature of God

STUDYQURAN:20:49/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r3.claim: If sincere, Pharaoh's question asks about God's modality, or how He is.
STUDYQURAN:20:49/r3.anchor: or how He is who He is.

SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r1.claim: Moses alone is addressed because he is the principal messenger, while Aaron is his follower, support, and minister.
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r1.anchor: قوله: { يموسى }: نادى موسى وحده بعد مخاطبته لهما معا: إما لأن موسى هو الأصل في الرسالة، وهارون تبع وردء ووزير

SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r2.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh knew Moses's speech impediment and Aaron's eloquence from 28:34 and 43:52, so he wanted Moses, not Aaron, to answer.
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r2.anchor: وإما لأن فرعون كان لخبثه يعلم الرتة التي في لسان موسى، ويعلم فصاحة أخيه بدليل قوله

SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r3.claim: He proposes ellipsis of the conjunction, with يا موسى meaning يا موسى وهارون.
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r3.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء، وبدأ به، ولا حاجة إليه، وقد يقال: حسن الحذف كون موسى فاصلة

SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r4.claim: The ellipsis is unnecessary, though it may suit the verse ending; one could instead say يا هارون وموسى, but addressing Moses first matters more.
SAMIN-DURR:20:49/r4.anchor: ولا حاجة إليه، وقد يقال: حسن الحذف كون موسى فاصلة، لا يقال: كان يغني في ذلك أن تقدم هارون

TAB-FULL:v16p79/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r1.claim: Although Pharaoh had addressed Moses and Aaron, he named Moses because one person answers on behalf of a group; the same narrative usage appears with the lost fish.
TAB-FULL:v16p79/r1.anchor: وإنما فعل ذلك كذلك، لأن المجاوبة إنما تكون من الواحد وإن كان الخطاب بالجماعة لا من الجميع

TABATABAI:20:49/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r1.claim: This section recounts Moses and Aaron's mission to Pharaoh, their signs and the magicians' defeat and conversion, then alludes to Israel's escape and Pharaoh's drowning.
TABATABAI:20:49/r1.anchor: بيان فصل آخر من قصة موسى عليه السلام يذكر فيه خبر ذهاب موسى وهارون عليهما السلام إلى فرعون وتبليغهما رسالة ربهما

TABATABAI:20:49/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r2.claim: The earlier command was to invite Pharaoh to monotheism and ask him to release Israel; their words are omitted, while Pharaoh's answer indicates what they said.
TABATABAI:20:49/r2.anchor: ما قالا له فهو محذوف وما نقل من كلام فرعون جوابا دال عليه

TABATABAI:20:49/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r3.claim: Pharaoh understood that both brothers shared the mission, with Moses leading and Aaron serving as his minister; he therefore addresses Moses but asks about their Lord together.
TABATABAI:20:49/r3.anchor: أنه علم بتعريفهما أنهما معا داعيان شريكان في الدعوة غير أن موسى هو الأصل في القيام بها وهارون وزيره

TABATABAI:20:49/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r4.claim: Pharaoh's own words show that he claimed to be the brothers' lord, as in his boast and threat elsewhere.

TABATABAI:20:49/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r5.claim: Although the brothers called God Pharaoh's Lord, Pharaoh feigns not to hear this and asks who their Lord is instead of asking who his own Lord is.
TABATABAI:20:49/r5.anchor: وكان الحري بالمقام أن يقول فمن ربي الذي تدعيانه ربا لي

TABATABAI:20:49/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r6.claim: In pagan thought, the creator was too transcendent for direct worship, so people worshiped created intermediaries to draw near to God and seek their intercession; these were called gods and lords.
TABATABAI:20:49/r6.anchor: بل الواجب التوجه إلى بعض مقربي خلقه بالعبادة والقربان ليقرب الإنسان من الله زلفى ويشفع له عنده

TABATABAI:20:49/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r7.claim: For idolaters, saying 'my lord' meant one of the subordinate gods, while God was the Lord of lords rather than a god or lord in their usage.
TABATABAI:20:49/r7.anchor: إنما يعني به أحد الآلهة من دون الله وليس يعني به الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:20:49/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49/r8.claim: Pharaoh's question does not deny the existence of the creator of all or that he himself has a deity.
TABATABAI:20:49/r8.anchor: ليس إنكارا لوجود خالق الكل ولا إنكار أن يكون له إله

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh's question about their Lord addresses Moses and Aaron through grammatical dominance of the dual; alternatively, Aaron's name was omitted for brevity and verse endings.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r6.anchor: وإنما قال ربكما على تغليب الخطاب

TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r7.claim: Pharaoh asks what kind of being their Lord is; Moses answers that God has no genus and is known through His acts.
TABRISI:20:52-53#2/r7.anchor: فبين موسى أنه تعالى ليس له جنس وإنما يعرف سبحانه بأفعاله

THALABI:v6p246/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p246/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p246/r11.claim: Pharaoh's question addresses both Moses and Aaron, but names Moses alone to preserve the verse-end rhyme.
THALABI:v6p246/r11.anchor: يعني يا موسى وهارون فذكر موسى دون هارون لرؤوس الآي.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq infers that Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and addressed him as God had reported, since Pharaoh then asks Moses who their Lord is.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (المعنى فأتياه فقالا له ما أخبر الله في كتابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r2.claim: One reading is that Pharaoh asks Moses about both Moses' and Aaron's Lord, but uses the singular address because Moses alone is being addressed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أن المعنى فمن ربك وربه يا موسى، فغلب الخطاب؛ لأن المخاطب كان موسى دون هارون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r3.claim: A second reading addresses both brothers while omitting Aaron's name to suffice with Moses and to match the verse endings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p413#2/r3.anchor: [الثاني: أن كليهما مخاطب، ترك ذكر هارون]

BURHAN:v3p334/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p334/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p334/r3.claim: The Qur’an shifts from addressing two people to one, as when Pharaoh asks the pair who their Lord is but names Moses, and when Adam and Eve are told فتشقى.
BURHAN:v3p334/r3.anchor: الثالث من الاثنين إلى الواحد كقوله

BURHAN:v2p240/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p240/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v2p240/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Pharaoh singles Moses out because he bears the great message and distinguished signs.
BURHAN:v2p240/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه افرد موسى عليه السلام بالنداء بمعنى التخصيص والتوقف

BURHAN:v2p240/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p240/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
BURHAN:v2p240/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's alternative explanation invokes the Qur'an's statement that Aaron was more eloquent than Moses and the exchange with the challenger.
BURHAN:v2p240/r4.anchor: ذكره صاحب الكشاف وانظر إلى الفرق بين الجوابين

BURHAN:v2p246/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p246/r1.speaker: الثعلبي
BURHAN:v2p246/r1.claim: Al-Tha'labi calls this changing form of address al-mutalawwin; scholars of meanings call it iltifat, a topic the author says he will address later.

BURHAN:v3p126/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p126/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v3p126/r1.claim: When wording requires two things but mentions one, Ibn Atiyya says Pharaoh says only Moses because he is the main bearer of the message.
BURHAN:v3p126/r1.anchor: لأن موسى المقصود المتحمل أعباء الرسالة كذا قاله ابن عطية

BURHAN:v3p126/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p126/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p126/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Pharaoh began to add Aaron's name but refrained, wary of Aaron's eloquence and sharp reply.
BURHAN:v3p126/r2.anchor: وغاص الزمخشري فقال أراد أن يتم الكلام فيقول وهارون

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r4.speaker: التنوخي وابن الأثير
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r4.claim: A related address shift moves between singular, dual, and plural addressees; the listed cases include singular to dual, singular to plural, dual to singular or plural, and plural to singular.
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r4.anchor: ومن الاثنين إلى الواحد ﴿ فمن ربكما يا موسى ﴾ ﴿ فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى ﴾

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r5.claim: “Who is your Lord, Moses?” illustrates moving from a dual addressee to a singular one, one of the address shifts classed near to الالتفات.
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r5.anchor: ومن الاثنين إلى الواحد ﴿ فمن ربكما يا موسى ﴾

ITQAN:v3p90/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p90/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ITQAN:v3p90/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Pharaoh addresses two people with a singular vocative, singling out Moses because of their special relation through his upbringing.
ITQAN:v3p90/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه أفرده بالنداء لإدلاله عليه بالتربية

ITQAN:v3p90/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p90/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ITQAN:v3p90/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya’s other explanation is that Moses alone is named because he bears the mission and signs, while Aaron follows him.
ITQAN:v3p90/r4.anchor: والآخر لأنه صاحب الرسالة والآيات وهارون تبع له ذكره ابن عطية

ITQAN:v3p90/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p90/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p90/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari adds that Pharaoh avoided addressing Aaron because Aaron was more eloquent than Moses and Pharaoh feared his tongue.
ITQAN:v3p90/r5.anchor: وذكر في الكشاف آخر وهو أن هارون لما كان أفصح من موسى نكب فرعون عن خطابه

ITQAN:v3p91/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p91/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p91/r1.claim: The inverse address pattern also appears: a dual audience receives a singular form, as when Pharaoh asks Moses, ‘Who is your Lord?’ while addressing both brothers.
ITQAN:v3p91/r1.anchor: الثاني والعشرون عكسه نحو ﴿ فمن ربكما يا موسى ﴾

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites shifts in addressee, including a question to Moses and Aaron that names Moses alone, and a reference to humanity’s father Adam.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p176/r10.claim: The dual pronoun addresses Moses and Aaron even though the vocative names Moses alone.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.claim: Ta-Ha presents a joint mission: both are sent, answer in fear, receive reassurance, deliver the message, and are addressed by Pharaoh together, making Aaron Moses's partner in conveying the message.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.anchor: فقد أمر كلاً من موسى وهرون بالذهاب بآياته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r1.claim: The report describes the reader using an unordered surah sequence, apparently before Uthman sent standard codices to the provinces and required their order.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r1.anchor: إلى الآفاق بالمصاحف الأئمة المؤلفة على هذا الترتيب المشهور اليوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r2.claim: Aisha told him that beginning with any surah would not harm him, and said the first revelation containing Paradise and Hell could be started later in the codex.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r3.claim: If Aisha did not mean Surat Iqra by the first surah mentioning Paradise and Hell, Ibn Kathir allows that she meant the category of Mufassal surahs with promise and warning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r3.anchor: فقد يحتمل أنها أرادت اسم جنس لسور المفصل التي فيها الوعد والوعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that people first embraced faith, then received commands and prohibitions gradually, as an act of divine wisdom and mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r4.anchor: ثم لما انقاد الناس إلى التصديق أمروا ونهوا بالتدريج أولا فأولا وهذا من حكمة الله ورحمته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r5.claim: Surah order could be changed, but the arrangement of verses within each surah is fixed by the Prophet; Aisha therefore dictated her written surah verses instead of permitting changes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r5.anchor: أمر توقيفي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r6.claim: A sound report from Hudhayfa and Ibn Masud says the Prophet recited al-Baqara, al-Nisa, then Al Imran in night prayer, supporting flexible surah order.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r6.anchor: حديث حذيفة وابن مسعود، وهو في الصحيح أنه، عليه السلام، قرأ في قيام الليل بالبقرة ثم النساء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari argues that delaying an earlier surah or advancing a later one is like corrupting the arrangement of verses and letters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن الأنباري في كتاب الرد أنه قال: فمن أخر سورة مقدمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir says the familiar surah order in the Uthmanic codex appears partly to reflect Uthman's judgment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن ترتيب السور فيه منه ما هو رجع إلى رأي عثمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir points to Ibn Abbas's question to Uthman about omitting the basmala before Bara'a and classing al-Anfal among the long surahs as evidence of Uthman's judgment; he calls the report's chain good and strong.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r9.anchor: سؤال ابن عباس له في ترك البسملة في أول براءة، وذكره الأنفال من الطول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r10.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r10.claim: Ibn Kathir reports that Ali had resolved to arrange the Quran according to its order of revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p47#2/r10.anchor: وقد ذكرنا عن علي أنه كان قد عزم على ترتيب القرآن بحسب نزوله

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r3.claim: The address to Moses omits Aaron; the discourse supplies his name and the omission also maintains the verse endings.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r3.anchor: وتقديره: فمن ربكما يا موسى وهارون، فحذف لدلالة الكلام عليه واستواء رؤوس الآي

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r4.claim: One view is that Pharaoh asked who their Lord was in order to deny the message.

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r5.claim: Another view is that Pharaoh asked who had sent them.

JISHUMI:v7p4674/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r6.claim: A third reading of the narrative supplies an omitted visit: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and addressed him before he replied.
JISHUMI:v7p4674/r6.anchor: وقيل: في الكلام حذف كأنه قال: فأتياه وقالا له ذلك، فقال مجيبا

BURSEVI:v5p303/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p303/r1.claim: Kāshifī narrates that Moses and Aaron came before Pharaoh by God's command, identified themselves as messengers and called him to worship God; Pharaoh then asked who their Lord was.
BURSEVI:v5p303/r1.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (س موسى وهارون بحكم حضرت الهي

BURSEVI:v5p303/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p303/r2.claim: Man is interrogative here, meaning who.

BURSEVI:v5p303/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303/r3.speaker: غيره
BURSEVI:v5p303/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the question as following from their claim to be messengers: if so, they must identify the Lord who sent them; Pharaoh's arrogance explains why he does not ask who his own Lord is.
BURSEVI:v5p303/r3.anchor: وقال غيره الفاء لترتيب السؤال على ما سبق من كونهما رسولي ربهما

BURSEVI:v5p303/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303/r4.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p303/r4.claim: The Imam links Pharaoh's question to his earlier boast that he raised Moses as a child: Pharaoh treats himself as Moses' lord and asks why Moses calls him to another Lord.
BURSEVI:v5p303/r4.anchor: قال الإمام أثبت نفسه ربا في قوله : {ألم نربك فينا وليدا}

BURSEVI:v5p303/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p303/r5.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v5p303/r5.claim: Pharaoh addresses both brothers, then singles out Moses because he is the principal messenger and Aaron his minister and follower.
BURSEVI:v5p303/r5.anchor: خاطبهما ثم أفرد موسى إذ كان يعلم أن موسى هو الأصل في الباب
